classification.review_note: Deviation from Raoult's law and boiling-point change on mixing phenol and aniline is a Unit 1 (Solutions, non-ideal solutions) concept; phenol/aniline are only the components named.
Contrast between a non-volatile solute (KCl, boiling-point elevation) and a volatile solute (methyl alcohol, boiling-point lowering) is colligative/Raoult's-law content (Unit 1).
Vapour-pressure lowering (Raoult's law) of benzoic acid in benzene with dimerisation is a Unit 1 numerical; benzoic acid is only the solute named.
E°(Sc3+/Sc) value and noble-gas configuration of Sc3+ are Unit 4 (electronic configuration/ electrode potentials of transition elements).

FLAGGED AS AMBIGUOUS: 'Vitamin B12 is a complex compound of Co3+'. The question is framed around a coordination complex (Unit 5), but vitamin B12 itself is Biomolecules (Unit 10) content. Primary assignment: Coordination Compounds (the assessed fact is the Co3+ complex); retained with low confidence and flagged in the QA report.

Enantiomer properties (equal and opposite specific rotation). In the Class 12 syllabus, optical isomerism/enantiomers are introduced in Unit 6 (Haloalkanes, stereochemistry of SN reactions); no complex is involved, so Unit 5 optical isomerism is not the primary target.
Chirality is taught in Unit 6 (Haloalkanes, optical activity of 2-bromobutane/butan-2-ol); options mix alcohols and haloalkanes but the assessed concept is chirality (Unit 6).
Options are structure images (aryl/vinyl/alkyl halides); visually confirmed as halides. Relative reactivity towards nucleophilic substitution is Unit 6.
CH3Cl + NaI in dry acetone is the Finkelstein halogen-exchange reaction (Unit 6); acetone is only the solvent.
Preparation of alkyl halides from alcohols (PCl5/PCl3/SOCl2 comparison) is Unit 6 (methods of preparation of haloalkanes).

(a) drawing the structure of 4-bromo-3-methylpent-2-ene (haloalkene nomenclature) and (b) hydrolysis of chloroethane with aqueous KOH (nucleophilic substitution of a haloalkane) are both Unit 6 content.

Reaction (a) is an image (visually confirmed): 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene + NaOH (368 K) then H+ — nucleophilic aromatic substitution of an activated aryl halide (Unit 6); (b) HBr addition to 2-methylbut-2-ene gives a haloalkane (Markovnikov addition, Unit 6 preparation of haloalkanes from alkenes).
(a) chlorobutane + Na in dry ether is the Wurtz reaction (Unit 6); (b) boiling-point order of butane and 1-halobutanes is Unit 6 (physical properties of haloalkanes).
SN1/SN2, racemisation and inversion of configuration of C4H9Br isomers is Unit 6 (stereochemistry of nucleophilic substitution); the alcohol is only the product.
Bromination of an alkene/alkane (addition/halogenation giving haloalkane), racemic mixture definition and p-dichlorobenzene melting point are Unit 6 content.
All three subparts are Unit 6: o,p-directing (deactivating) halogens in electrophilic aromatic substitution, aryl halides not obtainable from phenol + HX/PX5, and chloroform storage (phosgene).
KCN vs AgCN ambident nucleophile behaviour in haloalkane reactions (alkyl cyanide vs isocyanide) is Unit 6.

Aspirin is obtained by acetylation of salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid); this preparation is given in the Phenols section of Unit 7 (acetylation of salicylic acid gives aspirin), not in the carboxylic-acids unit.
Reaction is an image (visually confirmed): benzyl phenyl ether + HI -> benzyl iodide + phenol, i.e. cleavage of ethers by HI (Unit 7, chemical properties of ethers).
Oxidation of propan-2-ol with CrO3 to propanone is Unit 7 (oxidation of alcohols: 2° alcohol -> ketone); propanal/propanone are option names.

(a) acidic-strength order of phenol, 4-nitrophenol and 2,4,6-trinitrophenol is Unit 7 (acidity of phenols); (b) is alcohol chemistry. 'Acidic strength' wording alone would suggest Unit 8, but the compounds are phenols.
All three subparts (carboxylic acids' higher boiling points, acidic alpha-hydrogens, nucleophilic addition to carbonyl) are Unit 8 content.
Nitrile + Grignard reagent followed by hydrolysis gives a ketone, which then forms an oxime with H2N-OH: carbonyl chemistry (Unit 8). The nitrile is a reactant, not the assessed concept.

(a) propanenitrile + phenylmagnesium bromide then hydrolysis gives a ketone (Unit 8 carbonyl chemistry); (b) CrO3/acetic anhydride oxidation of p-fluorotoluene gives p-fluorobenzaldehyde (side-chain oxidation to aldehyde, Unit 8); (c) phthalic acid + NH3 gives phthalimide (Unit 8).
Arranging chloro-substituted butanoic acids by acidic strength tests the inductive effect on carboxylic acids (Unit 8); the Cl substituents (images) are only substituents.
All three conversions (propanone->propan-2-ol reduction, ethanal->ethane reduction, sodium benzoate->benzene decarboxylation) are Unit 8 conversions of carbonyl compounds/carboxylic acids.
Reduction of a nitrile with LiAlH4 to a primary amine is a Unit 9 preparation-of-amines reaction (ethylamine is the product); 'Ethanal' is a distractor option.
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is a Unit 9 preparation of amines; the Reason's mention of aryl halides is supporting context, not the assessed concept.
Options are structure images; visually confirmed as substituted anilines/benzylamine (p-nitroaniline, benzylamine, p-toluidine, aniline). Strongest base = benzylamine; basicity of amines is Unit 9.
NaOBr with an amide (Hofmann bromamide degradation, carbonyl carbon lost as CO3^2-) is a Unit 9 preparation of amines from amides.
Carbylamine reaction (primary amine + CHCl3 + KOH -> isocyanide) is Unit 9; the carboxylic-acid/aldehyde options are distractors.
Ammonolysis of an alkyl halide (NH3 + excess ethyl chloride -> quaternary ammonium salt as main product) is a Unit 9 preparation of amines.
Acetamide + Br2 + aqueous KOH -> methanamine is the Hofmann bromamide degradation (Unit 9 preparation of amines).
Boiling points/intermolecular hydrogen bonding of amines (propylamine vs trimethylamine) is Unit 9 (physical properties of amines).
(b) nitromethane to methyl isocyanide proceeds via the carbylamine reaction (Unit 9); (a) is an equation image consistent with amine chemistry.
Reactions of benzenediazonium chloride (Sandmeyer to chlorobenzene, reduction to benzene, etc.) are Unit 9 (diazonium salts); chlorobenzene is only a product.

Both reaction sequences are images (visually confirmed). (a) aniline + (CH3CO)2O (acetylation) then Br2/CH3COOH (bromination) then H+ — reactions of aniline (Unit 9). (b) 2-bromo-4-nitrotoluene + Fe/HCl (reduction to amine), NaNO2/HCl at 273-278 K (diazotisation), H3PO2/H2O (diazonium replacement) — Unit 9 amine synthesis/diazonium chemistry. Primary chapter: Amines.
